main_statement.latex: \begin{theorem} Let H be the incidence graph of the 22 triples on 13 points in Table~\ref{tab:complex}. This bipartite graph has 35 vertices and 66 edges. There is a finite simple undirected graph G with at least one edge such that t(H,G)<p(G)^{66}. \end{theorem}
main_statement.paraphrase: Sidorenko's conjecture (every bipartite H with an edge satisfies t(H,G)>=p(G)^{e(H)} for all G) is false: an explicit 35-vertex, 66-edge connected bipartite H (the vertex-face incidence graph of a 22-triangle complex on 13 points) has strictly fewer homomorphisms into some finite simple host than the random-graph benchmark. Corollaries: the deficit can be amplified to any ratio c>0 (tensor powers), persists for injective copies at a positive limiting density (blow-ups), and H is not p-forcing at one p, refuting the Skokan-Thoma / Conlon-Fox-Sudakov forcing conjecture.

D.max_item: I07+I08 signed half-rank layer kernel / rank-layer sign model (N3 candidate, F5); I15 two-branch activation law with support forcing (N3 candidate, F3)

evidence.quote: Half rank is the key geometric constraint: when the difference between two point matrices is nonsingular, the two rank-r images through a common center are complementary, which relates their determinant signs.

caveats: Grades conditional on an unrefereed claim resolving a 35-year-old conjecture; trust rests on the Lean compile (pending).
Quick literature checks only (WebSearch snippets); full novelty grading is the novelty agent's task.

The kernel's raw material (symmetric-matrix association scheme, Lagrangian Grassmannian counting, Gauss sums, WL refinement) is all classical; D3 rests on the FUNCTION these pieces are assembled to perform (simulating a hypergraph-parity obstruction in an ordinary graph), which a strict judge may call a new bridge rather than a jump.

Downgrade to D2 if a precedent is found that uses association-scheme / quadratic-form kernels to engineer signed homomorphism-density corrections (e.g. in common-graph or step-Sidorenko work), or if experts regard the hypergraph-to-graph 'centre vertex' simulation as known folklore.

proof_architecture.claim: Fix the witness complex (22 triples, 13 points): each pair in two faces, connected face graph, six bit classes with spanning growth orders, separation a_e>=1/3 with one >1/3, WL-discrete incidence graph.

Rank-layer lemma (stated, proved in steps 6-8): products of signed half-rank kernels K_xi(X_i-Y_j) over random symmetric matrices converge to a sign model prod_j prod_pairs(1+c_0 eta_e xi xi) with independent eta_e; averaging gives a parity test of four incidence signs per fully active pair.
Typed activation kernel with zero first moments; coordinate expansion: t_{I,J}(W_q)=1+sum_{type maps} weights * C_A(a,b)+o(1) with all labels nonempty.
One coordinate per corner; two-branch base law (M_kappa vs Gamma_kappa) with one negative corner sign; support forcing gives the unique identity-type term -(theta/2)^66.

Pin types: colour-refinement scores make identity the unique maximizer of Q over all part-preserving maps; Gibbs priors + thinning with large rho make the averaged coefficient t_0<0; dilution (eps^13 vs eps^22) controls the transpose; crossed product gives a symmetric [0,1] kernel with t(H,U)<mu^66; sampling gives the finite host.

Transverse part of the rank-layer lemma: half-rank complementary images relate center ranks to pair determinant signs; centers counted via maximal isotropic subspaces of L=B_0^{-1}-B_1^{-1}; restriction signs concentrate at 1/2; joint pair signs asymptotically independent by Schur complements + Gauss sums.

Singular part, local: symmetric matrices -> graph Lagrangians (rank defect = intersection dimension); orbit masses q^{-C}; planted-law density ratio bounds each face factor by q^g with explicit gains.

Singular part, global: profile probability via six bit-class exposures and geometric mean; slack = sum S_j + separation excess; coercivity bounds pair dimensions; propagation over the connected face graph + an a_e>1/3 pair bounds them uniformly; choose D large to force equality profiles (c=0, h_e in {0,2}); span counts give strict decay; hence the rank-layer lemma.

Consequences: tensor powers / blow-ups (amplification, injective copies); interpolation W_s between host and rank-one perturbation gives a nonconstant graphon with t(K_2)=p, t(H)=p^66, refuting the forcing conjecture.

eureka_candidates.item: I07+I08 (+I25): signed half-rank layer kernel K_xi on symmetric matrices over F_q and the rank-layer sign-model limit
eureka_candidates.for: Nothing like it occurs in the goal (which mentions only H and G) or in L. It is the mechanism that makes the counterexample possible: a common 'center' matrix at half rank forces complementary images (I25), so a face of three incidences becomes a multiplicative constraint on the determinant signs of the three point-pair differences, and the pair signs are asymptotically independent. In effect it simulates, inside an ordinary bipartite homomorphism density, the kind of 3-wise parity obstruction that makes hypergraph Sidorenko fail (loose triangle), a transfer the field had no mechanism for. The rank-layer lemma is ~84% of the Lean code (by lines) and is the single analytic input of the construction. It is syntactically small (an indicator of a rank/sign layer) but hard to find.
eureka_candidates.against: Every raw ingredient is classical: the rank+discriminant relations form the Huo-Wan association scheme (cited by the paper itself), Lagrangian/graph-of-symmetric-map geometry and split-form counts are textbook (Taylor), the joint-sign independence is a Gauss-sum computation (Gowers-Wolf), and algebraic hosts built from quadratic characters (Paley graphs, norm graphs, random algebraic constructions) are standard in extremal graph theory. A strict judge could call it a new bridge (association schemes -> Sidorenko) rather than a new concept. Its downstream reuse beyond Sidorenko-type density questions is untested.
eureka_candidates.nearest_neighbour: Huo-Wan 1993 association scheme of symmetric matrices (same relation, no density use); hypergraph Sidorenko counterexamples (Sidorenko 1993 loose triangle; Conlon-Lee-Sidorenko arXiv:2307.04588, 3-partite tight cycles) for the parity idea; London's weighted-matrix counterexample for P_4 (non-graph inequality); Lovasz-Szegedy/Lovasz 2011 local analysis showing any counterexample kernel must be far from constant.
eureka_candidates.lit_check: WebSearch (2026-10-12): 'Sidorenko counterexample symmetric matrices finite field rank kernel', 'dual polar graph symmetric matrices half rank Lagrangian Grassmannian homomorphism density', 'Sidorenko incidence graph triangulation sphere', 'Sidorenko 3-uniform loose triangle parity': no prior use of rank-layer / Lagrangian kernels for homomorphism-density sign engineering found (snippet level). Wikipedia now reports OpenAI's claim only.

eureka_candidates.item: I15+I16 (+I12): two-branch activation law on M_kappa / Gamma_kappa with one negative corner sign; zero first moments; support forcing to a unique -(theta/2)^66 term
eureka_candidates.for: A finite gadget, invented for this H, that cancels every nonconstant first sign moment yet keeps a signed overlap moment. Together with the support identity cap_{kappa in U_g} M_kappa = U_g it makes the identity-type coefficient a single, negative product. It is the sole source of negativity in the proof, and it is not in the goal or in L. The paper's own text has no precedent cue.
eureka_candidates.against: Mixtures of branches with opposite biases to kill first moments are a routine design move in Fourier/moment engineering. The support argument is short and uses only 'each pair in two faces'. Only 8% of the Lean (1,915 lines). Highly specific to the complex, so a downstream speedup outside Sidorenko-type questions is unlikely; it may be a one-off device.
eureka_candidates.nearest_neighbour: second-order (local) Sidorenko expansions around the constant kernel (Lovasz 2011); sign-perturbation constructions in common/step-Sidorenko graph work (Kral', Martins, Pach, Wrochna 2019); Walsh-Fourier moment-matching designs.
eureka_candidates.lit_check: Covered by the same searches; no construction with branch-switched supports found (snippet level).

eureka_candidates.item: I03 (+I04/I05): the witness H, a 13-vertex triangulation of the 2-sphere (22 triangles) with a 3-bit face labelling whose six bit classes are spanning growth sequences
eureka_candidates.for: Judged against the problem as originally posed (Sidorenko: all bipartite H), the witness is not a subterm. No prior literature proposes sphere-triangulation incidence graphs as candidates (the smallest previously open case discussed is K_{5,5} minus C_10). The paper's degree checks show it escapes every known positive criterion (not weakly norming, fails Coregliano's degree counts, minimum degree 3).
eureka_candidates.against: As an object it belongs to a classical class: Levi graphs of triangulated surfaces (analyst observation: V-E+F=2, all links are cycles; the paper never says 'sphere'). Its properties are exactly the constraints the proof needs, so its discovery is probably a computer search downstream of I07/I15, not an independent idea. A witness is a single instance and cannot be reused downstream.
eureka_candidates.nearest_neighbour: incidence graphs of simplicial complexes and partial Steiner triple systems; K_{5,5} minus C_10 and the Mobius ladder as standard open cases.
eureka_candidates.lit_check: WebSearch 'Sidorenko conjecture incidence graph triangulation sphere candidate counterexample': nothing relevant.

eureka_candidates.item: I17+I18: pinning by colour-refinement vertex/pair scores plus Gibbs priors and thinning
eureka_candidates.for: It turns WL-discreteness of H into a weighting under which the identity type assignment dominates all part-preserving maps, repetitions included. The sum-of-squares round score -||h(f(u))||^2+2<h(f(u)),h(u)> is a neat identity. Without it the negative identity term could be swamped.
eureka_candidates.against: WL/equitable partitions and their LP and fractional-isomorphism duals are classical, exponential tilting is the Laplace principle, and the paper itself says it 'adapts' colour refinement.
eureka_candidates.nearest_neighbour: Tinhofer / Grohe-Kersting-Mladenov-Selman fractional isomorphism; Dell-Grohe-Rattan homomorphism indistinguishability; Boker WL for graphons.
eureka_candidates.lit_check: WebSearch 'color refinement Weisfeiler-Leman scores pin identity homomorphism weighted graph ... graphon': related WL-graphon work only; no identical scoring lemma found.

eureka_candidates.item: I35+I36+I38: profile cost by six bit-class exposure orders with a geometric mean, the separation surplus E from a_e>1/3, and propagation of a large pair dimension across the face graph
eureka_candidates.for: This is the device that controls the singular tail, the main technical obstruction (the normalised kernels grow like a power of q). The bit labelling is designed so that every pair is internal to at most two of the six classes (a_e>=1/3), and the surplus from one strictly separated pair kills the 'common intersection' mode via propagation.
eureka_candidates.against: Averaging several exposure or covering orders is Shearer / Hoelder fractional-cover reasoning. The coercivity and propagation steps are ordinary estimates.
eureka_candidates.nearest_neighbour: Shearer's lemma / fractional edge covers in homomorphism counting (Friedgut-Kahn, Galvin-Tetali); exposure-martingale counting.

correctness_audit.verdict: This is an extraordinary claim: it disproves a well-known 1986/1991 conjecture. The paper is compact (3.9k lines) and internally coherent at the level read. Sections complex and kernel were checked line by line. Transverse, orbits, planted and tail were read in full; the exponent algebra was spot-checked symbolically. No gap was found. Trust rests on the Lean formalization (23.8k lines, text-level clean, comparator statement faithful to the theorem); the compile result is pending from the orchestrator. If it compiles under the three standard axioms, Theorem 1 is certified independently of the paper's prose.

concerns: The result is unreviewed. Search finds only the Wikipedia mention of OpenAI's claim and no independent expert verification (2026-10-12).

The singular-tail sections (orbits/planted/tail) have many exponent inequalities and constants (342, 33M, 44C_*, 1641). They were spot-checked, not fully audited by hand. The paper notes that the local maximizing tuples need not be simultaneously realizable and that only necessary constraints are used, so the argument is an upper bound; it is plausible but intricate.

Wikipedia calls the counterexample 'constructive', which overstates it. H is explicit, but G is only shown to exist: D is huge (>=1642 in the paper; the Lean matrix size is 2*(2r) with r := singularTailThreshold >= 1642), q, eps and rho come from limits, and G is a random sample. No explicit host or density gap is computable from the paper.
The forcing and amplification corollaries are not in the Lean. They are short and standard, but uncertified.
